title: Period and index on real surfaces
summary: A roadmap for Benoist's period-index theorems for function fields of real surfaces: period equals index when the surface has no real points or the class vanishes at real points, the exact topological obstruction for unramified classes (index n or 2n), real Enriques surfaces, a Puiseux counterexample, and the u-invariant 4 of real surface function fields with its consequences for quadratic forms and degree-four del Pezzo surfaces over real curves. It builds the needed real-function-field theory and imports equivariant topology, real Noether–Lefschetz theory, cycle classes and period-index arithmetic from their owners.
readme:
**Purpose.** This roadmap plans Olivier Benoist's solution of the period-index problem for function fields of real algebraic surfaces (Publ. Math. IHÉS 130, 2019). Its end results are: period equals index for every Brauer class of ℝ(S) when S(ℝ) = ∅ (Theorem 0.3), and for every class unramified on a smooth surface U and vanishing at all real points of U (Theorem 0.4); a complete criterion for unramified classes on smooth projective real surfaces, with index n or 2n according to a mod-2 topological condition on the half-period class (Theorem 0.5); the classification of real Enriques surfaces carrying classes with period ≠ index (Theorem 0.6); a K3 surface over the real Puiseux field where the criterion fails (Proposition 0.7); and the consequences for quadratic forms: the Elman–Lam u-invariant of any field of transcendence degree 2 over ℝ is ≤ 4, and equal to 4 for function fields of real surfaces (Theorem 0.12), quadratic forms of rank ≥ 5 are isotropic over ℝ(S) when S(ℝ) = ∅ (Theorem 0.10), and degree-four del Pezzo surfaces over ℝ(C) have points when C(ℝ) = ∅ (Theorem 0.13).

**Scope.** Ten layers PI.0–PI.9. PI.0 is the real-function-field theory the proof needs and no roadmap yet owns (orderings, real closures, signatures, the Elman–Lam invariant, Witt, Springer, Amer–Brumer, Albert, Pfister's criterion); it was proposed for a separate roadmap QuadraticFormsRealFunctionFields and moves there if that roadmap is created. PI.1 sets up unramified loci, real evaluation, de Jong's theorem and the norm bound. PI.2 is Benoist's Hodge-theoretic proof of de Jong's theorem for unramified classes on complex surfaces. PI.3–PI.6 carry out the real argument: ramified double covers, the pulled-back class, Noether–Lefschetz loci, real-locus control and the degree-two splitting. PI.7 assembles the main theorems and the u-invariant applications, PI.8 proves the obstruction, PI.9 the examples.

**Conventions.** ℝ is the field of real numbers except in PI.0 and in the Puiseux example, where an arbitrary real closed field is allowed and named. G = Gal(ℂ/ℝ) acts on X(ℂ) with fixed locus X(ℝ); H^i(Y) means H^i(Y, 𝔽₂); ℤ(j) is ℤ with conjugation acting by (−1)^j (Benoist's i^jℤ); equivariant cohomology is Borel/Grothendieck equivariant sheaf cohomology (AlgebraicTopologyPartII). Br(X) = H²_ét(X, 𝔾_m) ⊂ Br(k(X)) for smooth integral X. Period is the order in Br, index the SemisimpleAlgebrasPartII class index. [ξ]_i denotes the degree-i real component of an equivariant class (restriction to X(ℝ), canonical decomposition, projection). The Elman–Lam invariant u(K) counts anisotropic forms of zero signature at every ordering.

**Sources.** Benoist 2019 (published version, read in full); Bochnak–Coste–Roy, *Real Algebraic Geometry* (maintainer-cleared copy); Elman–Karpenko–Merkurjev (free); Becher 2005 (free); cited inputs from de Jong 2004, Voisin 2006 (through HodgeStructuresPartII), Benoist–Wittenberg 2020, Bröcker 1980, Mangolte–van Hamel 1998, Colliot-Thélène–Parimala 1990 and Degtyarev–Kharlamov 1996.

**Layer overview.** PI.0 field theory → PI.1 setting → PI.2 complex unramified case → PI.3 double covers → PI.4 pullback → PI.5 Noether–Lefschetz → PI.6 splitting → PI.7 main theorems → PI.8 obstruction → PI.9 examples.

**Non-goals.** De Jong's theorem in positive characteristic and Lieblich's finite-field bound (background only); the general Propositions 4.4–4.5 and 6.6 beyond uniform real evaluation (recorded gaps); Lang's and Pfister's conjectures in higher dimension (stated, never used); the topological, Hodge-theoretic, cycle-class and purity foundations, which belong to AlgebraicTopologyPartII, HodgeStructuresPartII, MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles and PurityForFlatCohomology.

stages.title: Real function fields: orderings, real closures and the Elman–Lam invariant
stages.description: **Targets.** The space of orderings X_F of a field with the Harrison topology, its compactness and inverse limits; real closures at a specified ordering (built on upstream RealAlgebraicGeometry Layer 1, `exists_realClosure`); signatures of quadratic forms at orderings; the clopen locus of orderings where a Brauer class survives; the Elman–Lam u-invariant (zero total signature); a C₁ field has trivial Brauer group; the u-invariant of a real curve function field is ≤ 2; Witt's theorem on Brauer classes of real curves (classes vanishing at all real closures, or at a dense set of real points, are zero, ramified or not); Springer's theorem over complete discretely valued fields; the Amer–Brumer theorem; Albert's isotropy criterion for Albert forms; the Elman–Lam bound for fields with u(F(√−1)) ≤ 4; Pfister's criterion (index two for real-closure-trivial classes implies u ≤ 4) in transcendence degree 2. This layer is the real-function-field tranche that QuadraticFormInvariantsPartII proposed as QuadraticFormsRealFunctionFields; it never imports the applications of PI.7.

stages.title: Period, index and real evaluation on real surfaces
stages.description: **Targets.** The unramified locus U_α of a class of Br(ℝ(S)) (via purity, PurityForFlatCohomology PF.6); real evaluation and the clopen nonzero-evaluation locus Θ(α), with the degree-zero component of Kummer lifts; de Jong's period-index theorem in characteristic 0 (imported reduction, unramified case from PI.2); the norm bound ind | 2 per over any real closed base; extension of line bundles from dense opens and injectivity of H¹ under removal of finitely many points.

stages.title: Unramified classes on complex surfaces
stages.description: **Targets.** Benoist's Hodge-theoretic proof of de Jong's theorem for unramified classes: the hypersurface family in |dnH| on ℙ¹ × S, vanishing of the topological obstruction by weak Lefschetz, the compatible integral lift (reduction equal to p*α̃) and pushforward adjustment, density of splitting hypersurfaces via Voisin's kernel cone, and ind = per for α ∈ Br(S).

stages.title: Ramified double covers
stages.description: **Targets.** The finite rank-two cover Spec_S(O ⊕ L⁻¹(−R)) branched along R ∪ D (normal, ordinary double points over Sing Δ); the incidence model rv² = sw² in ℙ_S(O ⊕ L), its map to the finite model, its fixed singular centres (w = 0 over Sing R) and resolution, the family in a fixed threefold; local structure and Stein factorisation p_*O_T = O_S ⊕ L⁻¹(−R); étale and finite-flat strata; p_* is an isomorphism on H^{≥3} and onto on H² for L(R) ample; the image of the equivariant pushforward is cut out by the first real component.

stages.title: Pulling back a period-two class to a double cover
stages.description: **Targets.** Assumption 4.1 on the cover (avoidance of Ψ ⊃ Θ, kernel generation, H² injectivity); the pulled-back class is unramified; its topological obstruction is killed by ω; uniform-evaluation forms of Propositions 4.4–4.5 (obstruction vanishing, trace-quotient Picard correction, curve adjustment, integral pushforward adjustment); the general Propositions 4.4–4.5 as stated, with their recorded gap.

stages.title: Noether–Lefschetz loci for double covers
stages.description: **Targets.** Assumption 5.1 and the real-pointless curve C; the point s = a₁s₀ + a₂c of B and the lift of C to T; restriction of the anti-invariant summand to C; Assumption 5.2; h¹(C, N_{C/X}) ≤ h²(O_S) and H²(T, O_T(C)) = 0; dim coker φ_λ ≤ h²(O_S); blowing up points to realise Assumption 5.2.

stages.title: Real-locus control and the degree-two splitting
stages.description: **Targets.** Positivity in squared lines; Assumption 6.1 on the real branch locus, its stability and its realisation after blow-ups; Nash approximation (BCR 12.4.11) and Bröcker's real divisors as cited inputs; the signed branch section t with real divisor H − R corrected; Assumption 6.1 implies Assumption 4.1; the vanishing variation and surjectivity of the Gauss–Manin derivative; normalisation and transport of the Kummer lift; Proposition 6.6 in the uniform-evaluation form, and as stated.

stages.title: Period equals index: the main theorems and the u-invariant
stages.description: **Targets.** Uniform evaluation of the half-period class; the induction step and Proposition 6.7; Theorem 0.3 (S(ℝ) = ∅), Theorem 0.4 (zero real evaluation), the sufficient half of Theorem 0.5; real-closure triviality implies pointwise triviality; Theorem 0.12 (u(K) ≤ 4 in transcendence degree 2, u(ℝ(S)) = 4 with the corrected anisotropic witness); Theorem 0.10 (rank ≥ 5 forms isotropic when S(ℝ) = ∅); Theorem 0.13 (degree-four del Pezzo surfaces over ℝ(C) with C(ℝ) = ∅ have points).

stages.title: The obstruction to period equals index
stages.description: **Targets.** The finite-flat open U₀ and Θ₀; the alternating double cover and branch multiplicities; the trace-quotient lift and the sign-corrected pullback lift; the circle double cover and its local monodromy correction; the correcting line bundle and algebraicity of the quotient component; Proposition 7.1 (even-degree splitting obstruction) and the obstruction half of Theorem 0.5 (ind = 2 per).

stages.title: Real Enriques surfaces and the Puiseux counterexample
stages.description: **Targets.** The image of the first two real components (Proposition 8.1); real Enriques surfaces and their halves, the Brauer group killed by 4, period-four classes, the real Picard image (cited), the half detector, and Theorem 0.6; the field of real Puiseux series, the sextic double plane and its K3 resolution with four sphere components, a class evaluating to zero on exactly one component, the quaternion sign contradiction, and Proposition 0.7.
